Events that disagree with M3: what they are

Golden June bench rows under the physical RC model (finalize_phys, lxplus), every event looked at through its waveforms, the M3 cluster trees rebuilt from raw, and a two-chamber cross-check. Plus det4 at H4. rerun/outliers/, 2026-10-25.

Verdict. On det3, 11.8 % of M3-matched events disagree with M3 (angle > 5° or position > 3 mm, or rejected for competing clusters). The M3 reference is at fault in about 0.8 %, almost all of it bent tracks: a muon that scatters between the M3 doublets leaves the straight 4-layer line several mm off at the DUT with χ² still inside the cut. Showers and multi-particle events are not M3 failures: M3 sits on one of the particles every time, and the MX17 fit takes the other (3.0 % with delta rays). Geometry (tracks outside the active area, the drift-field distortion within 20 mm of an X edge) is 4.1 %, MX17 response/reconstruction on clean tracks 2.2 %, and 1.8 % are correct fits removed by the competing-cluster cut.

det4 / det7 head-on. Their head-on far tail is explained by hardware already known: det7 X card 1 (x < 199 mm, the asterisk) and det4's dead amplification bands, plus the edge zone. Without those, head-on far is det4 2.5 / 3.8 %, det7 2.1 / 2.2 % (X / Y), against det3 2.6 / 2.5 %. The +1.4–3.6 pp the physical model added on det4 is mostly low-charge events in dead bands. det7 was never at SPS. det4 at H4 is not answered yet: the same fitter with the bench-calibrated phys bundle gives head-on far X 17.4 ± 1.3 %, Y 14.8 ± 1.3 % on run_71 (bench det4 under the same script: X 14.7 ± 1.5 %, Y 13.7 ± 1.2 %), but the beam waveforms are not what that bundle describes (a lumpy 2 µs column in wet CF₄, a strongly one-sided delayed X copy), so this is a model failure, not a detector rate. It needs a beam bundle (re-run plan S4).

Matched events: det3 7093, det4 7780, det7 8000, det6 8000, det2 3666. Classes are assigned in the order of the table (first match wins), from waveform features over the full plane (charge on the M3 footprint, other clusters, cluster width, saturation), the M3 cluster trees, and the active area; every class was checked by eye on random displays (below). POS_TAIL is split into bent / MX17 by the mixture fit described in the M3 section.

  • det7 X: far share 40–70 % for x < 199 mm (card 1, M1 badly seated: the asterisk), 5–10 % on card 2. On card 2 det7 behaves like det3.
  • det4: far share follows the amplification stripes in x, in both views (the stripes are in the amplification gap). Inside the live bands det4 head-on far is 5.9 % X / 8.7 % Y (bench), vs 3.6 / 3.2 % on det3 interior. What remains is low-gain partial columns and clean-track fit failures (FIT column).
  • The phys increment (+2.7 pp X, +3.6 pp Y head-on on det4): 52–56 % of the newly far events sit in dead bands, at 0.55× the median charge; timeD fitted them at |tan| ≈ 0.04, phys tilts them to ≈ 0.2. The narrow physical footprint makes faint, partial columns tilt. On det7 the increment is edge (23–36 %) and saturated wide clusters.

Edge zone: the drift field bends near the cage walls (PAPER_PLAN D4, re-measured on wft angles)

det3 X: the angle response k (fitted tan / M3 tan) is 0.62 at 5–10 mm from the X edge, 0.58 at 10–15, 0.90 at 15–20 and 1.0 beyond 20 mm; far share 86 / 41 / 6 %. Head-on tracks there read a fake tilt of 0.10–0.15 in tan (6–9°) within 10 mm and ~0.06 at 10–20 mm, with deep charge pulled inward at both edges (det3 and det6 X). det3 Y shows nothing: the Y strip plane is passivated for 18 mm at each edge, so Y never sees the wall region. det2 (chamber B, degrador rings removed) has the opposite sign in Y (outward) and the strongest effect. This replaces the hits-era −3° (δ ≈ −0.06 tan, ≲ 25–40 mm). It is most of det3's head-on excess: inside 20 mm of the edges det3 head-on and inclined far rates are equal.

The two-track fit splits 8 % of the MULTI views and raises their agreement with M3 from 22 to 25 %; dropping the split threshold ten-fold (F 30) changes nothing further. The right track is usually already among the candidates (MULTI "any" ≈ 70 %): the limit is the choice, not the splitting. No reference-free rule takes it without cost: lowest χ²/dof reaches ~50 % on MULTI but moves ~27 % of the correct competing-cluster fits off M3. Controls are untouched in every arm.

When is M3 wrong? Bent tracks, and nothing else of size

The tracker writes only the best ray. Its cluster trees (all clusters on all 8 planes) were rebuilt from the raw files with the production chain (condor 4546889; rays bit-identical to production, 12 977/12 977 on det3 file 000) to look for wrong cluster combinations, ghosts and kinks.

  • Wrong combination / ghosts: an alternative M3 combination pointing at the MX17 particle explains 0.01 % of det3 events. In MULTI events, a second M3 track matching the second MX17 particle exists in 0–1 % of cases. The extra particles are local (secondaries near the chamber), and M3 is on the muon.
  • Bent tracks: with 2 + 2 layers, the 4-point fit barely notices a kink between the doublets. A 12 mrad scatter near the DUT moves the line 3.5 mm at the DUT with χ² = 0.5 mm², inside the χ² < 1 cut. The POS_TAIL events (clean single track, angle right, > 3 mm off) have M3 χ² 0.37 vs 0.14 for clean events and doublet kinks of 6–9 mrad vs 3–4. Their residual follows the kink, and MX17 sits on the doublet vertex (median |res| 3.7 → 1.5 mm; the vertex predictor's own spread is 1.6 mm). A mixture fit gives the bent share det3 0.67 ± 0.06, det4 0.46 ± 0.13, det7 0.44 ± 0.11, det6 0.00 ± 0.12, det2 0.49 ± 0.11. det6 sits at z = 232, close to the lower doublet, where such a kink does not move the M3 line; its zero is the control.
  • Two chambers at once (6-26 night, det6 + det7, 1631 clean events): in six-point lines the single odd point above χ² 50 is always an MX17 chamber ({'det7': 61, 'det6': 49}). That alone does not convict MX17, because the middle of the lever arm is exactly where a scattered track leaves the chord, and that is where det7 is. At milder χ² an M3 layer is the odd point ({'det7': 268, 'L3': 172, 'det6': 121, 'L0': 118, 'L2': 88, 'L1': 86}), with shifts ≲ 1.5 mm.
  • A kink-corrected reference (MX17 − M3 − β·kink, cross-validated) moves the core resolution by ≤ 0.03 mm: the doublet kink is measured too coarsely (~4 mrad) to correct single events.

SPS: det4 at H4

run_71 RAW, flat mount, 700 V drift plateau (233 V/cm, v = 14.0 µm/ns from the CF₄-epoch timing), uRWELL reference (truth tan = 0, divergence 0.5 mrad), both views ±8 strips around the reference. Same pivot fitter and det4 phys bundle (beam D_rc), 64 samples, K = 40, Dp 0.015 (the wet-CF₄ value is not measured). The bench rows use the same script on the held-out head-on events of the vladder caches.

Reading. The H4 tails are symmetric, wide (5th/95th percentile −23° / +32° on X), on high-charge unsaturated events; 150 GeV beam particles barely scatter. The waveforms show why: the drift column is there (charge spans 0.95 × the expected 2.1 µs) but its charge sits in one to three short bright bursts, and X carries the one-sided delayed ±1 copy (0.26 prompt / 0.40 delayed, plane_ratio README) that the symmetric bench kernel lacks. A bench bundle with only v, Dp and the sample count changed does not describe this, so the far fraction measures the model mismatch. A K = 24 first attempt was also wrong (the depth grid did not cover the 2.1 µs column, C5); the table is K = 40. Not a measurement of det4.

Pogo check on the beam data (rerun/pogo_check/run_sps.py, det4 FEU 03 renumbered to M1 channels; connectors 3–6 = both cards): X ['CLEAN', 'CLEAN'], Y ['CLEAN', 'CLEAN'], 0 cross-card links. Only the beam-lit channels are testable (98 of 256 on X, 201 on Y fired ≥ 50 times). The bench golden rows were already checked: only det7 X card 1 is POGO.

What each class looks like

Four random events per class. Per view: strip position × time over ±30 mm (red dashed: M3, white: the fit), and the strip maximum over the whole plane.

det3 MULTI: two particles; M3 on one, the fit on the other.
det3 DELTA: a delta ray branching off the muon.
det3 POS_TAIL: clean track parallel to M3, 3–4 mm away (mostly bent tracks).
det3 EDGE: within 20 mm of an edge.
det3 FIT_SAT: clean saturated track, wrong fit.
det3 FIT: clean track, wrong fit.
det3 OUTSIDE: M3 outside the active area; the fit found something else.
det3 REJECTED_OK: the fit agrees, the competing-cluster cut removed it.
det4 dead bands: no or partial column.
det4 FIT in live bands.
det7 X card 1.
det7 MULTI.

What this does not rule out

  • The bent-track share is a mixture fit on 35–90 events per chamber; the per-event call is not possible (the doublet vertex is only good to 1.6 mm). The rest of POS_TAIL (det3 ~0.4 % of events) may be MX17 response or kinks away from the DUT.
  • Classes are assigned in a fixed order; an event with two causes counts once (e.g. a second particle near an edge is EDGE). HW_KNOWN on det7 is event-level: a Y-view outlier in an event whose X sits on card 1 counts there.
  • The edge zone is defined at 30 mm from the measured k(distance) (bands 0–5 … 20–30 mm, see the follow-ups); the edge-zone sign difference on det2 (degrador removed) is one chamber.
  • SPS: the head-on question is open for det4 (no beam-calibrated bundle; the attempt here fails on the model). det4's beam spot sits on a live band, so a future SPS number tests det4's live area only. det7 was never at SPS.
  • The bench second-particle rate (2–4 %) includes secondaries from the stand and the other chamber; it is a property of the bench, not of n_TOF.
  • Waveform displays use the local decoded_root (det4 6-24: the pre-fa80c06 decode; fused events are skipped).
